predictions.selection_reason: user-controlled property name -> embedded in property access code -> potential prototype pollution if not properly escaped
predictions.source_summary: Property name comes from node.index.getObjectProperty() which extracts value from ConstantNode dimensions in IndexNode. User input flows through expression parsing to create these nodes.
predictions.sink_summary: Property access via getSafeProperty function which validates object type and property ownership before access.
predictions.guard_summary: getSafeProperty enforces: 1) object must be plain object (isPlainObject check), 2) property must be own property (Object.hasOwnProperty check), 3) blocks access to constructor method, 4) uses safeMethods whitelist for function properties. Property name is stringified with escaping.
predictions.risk_pattern: User-controlled property names are validated through getSafeProperty's security controls before property access, preventing prototype pollution and unauthorized method access.
predictions.context_summary: Compiles object property access expressions to JavaScript code. When accessing object properties (not array indices), uses getSafeProperty wrapper for security validation.
unresolved_facts: Exact user input flow path from parser to AccessorNode creation
Whether all user input paths properly validate property names before reaching getSafeProperty

retrieval_query.mechanism_summary: bypass of getSafeProperty validation through property name manipulation
retrieval_query.source: user-controlled property names in object access
retrieval_query.missing_control: insufficient validation of property names before getSafeProperty
retrieval_query.impact: prototype pollution via __proto__ or constructor properties

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
top_sast_rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-1321 prototype-pollution __proto__ constructor prototype object-key property-key merge assign recursive-merge
top_sast_rules.remediation: Reject prototype keys and use schema-constrained object updates.

top_sast_rules.description: If an object literal has two properties with the same name, the second property overwrites the first one, which makes the code hard to understand and error-prone.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Remove unused variables that may contain sensitive data. Use static analysis tools to identify unused code. Review code for potential logic errors.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
top_sast_rules.description: Modifying an object obtained via a user-controlled property name may lead to accidental mutation of the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement proper output encoding based on context (HTML, JavaScript, CSS, URL). Use Content Security Policy and validate input.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
top_sast_rules.description: When escaping special characters using a meta-character like backslash or ampersand, the meta-character has to be escaped first to avoid double-escaping, and conversely it has to be unescaped last to avoid double-unescaping.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Detect output operations that lack proper encoding for the target context
top_sast_rules.remediation: Use context-appropriate encoding for all output operations. Implement proper escaping for HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and URL contexts.
